summary: LunarSite Scout is a web dashboard that helps mission planners evaluate and compare candidate landing sites near the Moon's south pole for NASA Artemis and CLPS missions. Choosing a site means balancing many factors at once: terrain slope, illumination, Earth communication visibility, and proximity to permanently shadowed regions that may hold water ice. This data is scattered across datasets and hard to compare side by side. Our tool brings NASA lunar data into one interface where users can inspect each site, compare candidates, and see how they rank against mission criteria. This makes early-stage site selection faster, clearer, and more transparent. Better landing site decisions reduce mission risk and support sustainable exploration and resource utilization at the lunar south pole.
details: Lunar Site Scout is an interactive dashboard for evaluating and comparing lunar south pole landing sites. Users can browse candidate sites, view key metrics, and compare them side by side to find the best fit for a mission. Benefits and impact: It cuts the time needed to compare sites, makes tradeoffs transparent, and supports safer, better-informed decisions for Artemis and CLPS-style missions. It also works as an educational tool for students and the public. Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, deployed on Vercel. Data sources are NASA lunar datasets (listed below). Creativity: We turned complex multi-factor site selection into one comparison view that non-experts can use. Factors considered: Terrain and slope, illumination, communication visibility, proximity to water-ice regions, and mission relevance
